summary: ITC's revenue and profit have grown more slowly than the other stocks reviewed so far — a 3.6% revenue CAGR and 2.5% net income CAGR over FY23-FY26 — consistent with its position as a mature, diversified conglomerate (cigarettes, FMCG, paperboards, agri, and until recently hotels) rather than a growth story. One year stands out: net income jumped enough to push ROE to 49.6% in FY25 before falling back to 28.5% in FY26 — a swing that size usually reflects a one-time item (ITC demerged its hotels business around this period, which can produce exactly this kind of one-off gain), though this data alone can't confirm the cause. Debt is negligible (0.03x debt-to-equity) and free cash flow has stayed consistently positive and growing.
